reasoning_summary: The fix involves changing the value assigned to the 'double.class' key in the 'primitiveValues' map from an integer '0' to a double '0D'. This is a classic case of an incorrect initialization value for a specific type, which caused type mismatch errors during runtime.
evidence_used: The fix diff shows: - primitiveValues.put(double.class, 0); + primitiveValues.put(double.class, 0D);
The failing tests reported 'java.lang.ClassCastException: class java.lang.Integer cannot be cast to class java.lang.Double' and 'expected:<0.0> but was:<0>'.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is a simple correction of a single value in a map initialization, not a change to the logic or algorithm of the method.
